headline: Stocks Hold Broad Gains at Midday as Homebuilders and Healthcare Lead
body_html:
Stocks are comfortably higher at midday Tuesday, with 401 of the 544 names we track rising and 140 falling. Prices are not final. Seven of the eight groups we follow are in the green, and energy is the only laggard, off a marginal 0.09%.

Homebuilders lead at 2.4%, a notable showing given that single-family housing starts and permits fell sharply in September. Investors seem willing to look past the weak report. Healthcare is up 1.86% and software 1.38%. Sarepta Therapeutics is the standout, up 7.95%, with argenx up 6.28% and Hims & Hers Health up 5.97%. Fresh late-stage obesity-drug data from Novo has also kept attention on the sector.

The weak spots are concentrated in industrial and infrastructure names. Mueller Industries is down 8.76%, Boot Barn 4.73%, Comfort Systems USA 3.89% and Quanta Services 2.97%. Gulf tensions are another backdrop, after most regional bourses fell on reported Houthi attacks on Saudi sites. Into the close, traders will watch whether the advance holds and how the market reacts to SpaceX results after the bell, ahead of Wednesday, October 21.

briefs.headline: Biotech Pops Lead the Healthcare Charge
briefs.body: Healthcare is up 1.86% at midday, with Sarepta Therapeutics ahead 7.95% and argenx up 6.28%. Hims & Hers Health has added 5.97%. Novo's late-stage obesity data, which showed 25% weight loss in women, adds to the positive tone around the group.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Rally Despite Soft Housing Data
briefs.body: Homebuilders are the top group at 2.4%, even though September single-family starts and building permits dropped sharply. The market appears to be reading the weak data as something to look past. Whether the gains survive into the close is a key test.

briefs.headline: Industrial and Infrastructure Names Under Pressure
briefs.body: Mueller Industries is the biggest decliner we track, down 8.76%. Comfort Systems USA is off 3.89%, Quanta Services 2.97% and ABB 3.79%. The weakness stands out against a broadly firm tape, with industrials as a group still up 0.5%.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Slip on Houthi Attack Claims
briefs.body: Most Gulf bourses are lower after the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy and airport sites. Britain said it will fly defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia. Energy is the only one of our eight groups in negative territory, down 0.09%.

briefs.headline: Data Center Stocks Slide After Korean IPO Plunge
briefs.body: Data center shares are under pressure after a Korean IPO fell 30%, weighing on tech sentiment. Semiconductors are still up 0.87% and software 1.38%. Separately, Anthropic is reportedly in talks with Nscale on a second deal.

briefs.headline: SpaceX Earnings Set the Tone After the Bell
briefs.body: SpaceX reports after the close, and options traders are positioning for a notable move. Investors are also counting on earnings season to reset the bull market, with attention on a key S&P 500 level. Wednesday, October 21 will show whether today's gains carry over.
